Bengaluru is witnessing a huge high-rise boom with many skyscrapers being built in different parts of the city. Being the technology capital of India makes it one of the fastest growing mega cities in the world. The influx of high-skilled individuals from all parts of India come here for job and business opportunities. This is the reason why there is always demand for office and living space within the city and as a result Bengaluru is moving towards vertical development. CNTC Presidential Tower (topped-out in early 2023) is currently the tallest building in the city. It is 161 metres (528 ft) tall and has 50 floors. - Became tallest in 2022

**Previous record holders:**
- World One: 280.2 metres (919 ft), 76 floors (2020-2022)
- Imperial Towers: 256 metres (840 ft), 60 floors (2010-2020)

## **Delhi-NCR**

- Topped out in 2022

## **Bengaluru (Bangalore)**
**CNTC Presidential Tower** - 161 metres (528 ft), 50 floors
- Currently the tallest building in Bengaluru
- Topped out in early 2023

**Previous record holders:**
- Mantri DSK Pinnacle: 153 metres (502 ft), 46 floors (2013-2023)
- World Trade Center Bangalore: 128 metres (420 ft), 32 floors (2010-2013)

## **Hyderabad**
**Lodha Bellezza Towers 3, 4 & 5** - 153 metres (502 ft), 45 floors
- Currently the tallest completed buildings in Hyderabad
- As of January 2023

**Notable under-construction project:**

## **Ahmedabad**
**World Centre – 3** - 142 metres (466 ft)
- tallest commercial building

**Tallest residential building:**
**Takshashila AIR** - 115 metres (377 ft)

2. **Delhi-NCR** has the second tallest (Supernova Spira at 300m)

4. **Ahmedabad's tallest buildings** are relatively shorter compared to other major cities
5. There's significant vertical development happening across all these cities, with numerous supertall projects approved and under construction

The data reflects the ongoing construction boom in India's major metropolitan areas, driven by urbanization and the demand for premium commercial and residential spaces.
